name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q01 - Symmetry and water canal system in Porifera

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Sponges are mostly asymmetrical and exhibit cellular level of organisation.

Statement II: Water enters the sponge body through minute pores called ostia into the spongocoel and exits through the osculum.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Members of Phylum Porifera (sponges) are primitive multicellular animals characterised by loose cell aggregates and a water transport (canal) system.

Step 2: Evaluation
Sponges are mostly asymmetrical and exhibit the cellular level of organisation, so the first claim is true. Furthermore, their water transport pathway involves entry of water through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into the central spongocoel, followed by exit through the osculum, so the second claim is also true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q02 - Germinal layers and metagenesis in Coelenterata

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Coelenterates are diploblastic animals with an undifferentiated layer called mesoglea between the ectoderm and endoderm.

Statement II: All coelenterates exhibit alternation of generation (metagenesis) between polyp and medusa forms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Coelenterates (Cnidarians) are diploblastic animals with tissue level of organisation and two basic body forms: polyp and medusa.

Step 2: Evaluation
Coelenterates possess an external ectoderm, an internal endoderm, and an undifferentiated mesoglea between them, making the first claim true. However, only those cnidarians that exist in both polyp and medusa forms (such as Obelia) exhibit metagenesis, whereas forms like Hydra and Adamsia exist only as polyps and Aurelia exists as medusa; thus, the second claim is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q03 - Symmetry, coelom, and flame cells in Platyhelminthes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Platyhelminthes are radially symmetrical, triploblastic, and pseudocoelomate animals.

Statement II: Specialised cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flatworms (Phylum Platyhelminthes) have dorso-ventrally flattened bodies and organ level of organisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, and acoelomate (not radially symmetrical or pseudocoelomate), so the first claim is false. On the other hand, specialised flame cells indeed perform osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes, so the second claim is true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q04 - Reproduction and fertilisation in Ctenophora

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Phylum Ctenophora, reproduction takes place by both asexual fragmentation and sexual means.

Statement II: Ctenophores have separate sexes and undergo internal fertilisation with direct development.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ctenophores (sea walnuts or comb jellies) are exclusively marine, diploblastic organisms with distinct reproductive traits.

Step 2: Evaluation
In ctenophores, reproduction takes place only by sexual means (not asexual fragmentation), making the first claim false. Moreover, sexes are not separate in ctenophores, fertilisation is external, and development is indirect, making the second claim false as well.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q05 - Digestive tract and sexual dimorphism in Aschelminthes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Aschelminthes, the alimentary canal is complete with a well-developed muscular pharynx.

Statement II: Aschelminthes are dioecious (sexes are separate), and females are often longer than males.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aschelminthes (roundworms) are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, pseudocoelomate animals with organ-system level of organisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Roundworms possess a complete alimentary canal equipped with a well-developed muscular pharynx, so the first claim is true. Additionally, sexes are separate (dioecious) with distinct males and females, and females are often longer than males, so the second claim is also true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q06 - Musculature, circulation, and sexuality in Annelida

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Annelids possess longitudinal and circular muscles for locomotion and have a closed circulatory system.

Statement II: Earthworms and leeches are dioecious, whereas aquatic annelids like Nereis are monoecious.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Annelida consists of metamerically segmented coelomates with well-developed muscular, circulatory, and reproductive systems.

Step 2: Evaluation
Annelids possess both longitudinal and circular muscles that aid in locomotion and exhibit a closed circulatory system, making the first claim true. However, Nereis (an aquatic annelid) is dioecious, whereas earthworms and leeches are monoecious (hermaphrodite), making the second claim false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q07 - Exoskeleton, circulation, and excretion in Arthropoda

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Arthropods have a calcareous shell, an unsegmented body, and a closed circulatory system.

Statement II: In arthropods, excretion takes place through Malpighian tubules and statocysts function as balancing organs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Arthropoda is characterised by jointed appendages, a chitinous exoskeleton, and an open circulatory system.

Step 2: Evaluation
Arthropods have a chitinous exoskeleton (not a calcareous shell), a segmented body divided into head, thorax, and abdomen (not unsegmented), and an open circulatory system (not closed), so the first claim is false. On the other hand, Malpighian tubules carry out excretion and statocysts act as balancing organs in arthropods, so the second claim is true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q08 - Body plan and radula in Mollusca

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Molluscs are pseudocoelomate animals with metamerically segmented bodies.

Statement II: The radula in molluscs is a respiratory organ located inside the mantle cavity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Mollusca includes soft-bodied coelomates with a distinct head, muscular foot, and visceral hump.

Step 2: Evaluation
Molluscs are true coelomates with an unsegmented body (not pseudocoelomate or metamerically segmented), so the first claim is false. Furthermore, the radula is a file-like rasping organ for feeding located in the mouth, whereas feather-like gills in the mantle cavity perform respiration and excretion, so the second claim is also false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q09 - Symmetry, endoskeleton, and excretion in Echinodermata

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical, whereas their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

Statement II: Echinoderms possess an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and lack an excretory system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Echinodermata comprises exclusively marine coelomates with a calcareous endoskeleton and stage-dependent body symmetry.

Step 2: Evaluation
Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry while their free-swimming larvae exhibit bilateral symmetry, making the first claim true. They also possess an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and completely lack an excretory system, making the second claim true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q10 - Taxonomic position and physiology of Hemichordata

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hemichordata is now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata, although its members possess a rudimentary stomochord in the collar region.

Statement II: Hemichordates have a closed circulatory system and excrete wastes through nephridia.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hemichordata was earlier considered a sub-phylum under Chordata due to the stomochord, but is now classified as a separate non-chordate phylum.

Step 2: Evaluation
Hemichordates are placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata and possess a rudimentary stomochord (similar to a notochord) in the collar region, making the first claim true. However, their circulatory system is of the open type and their excretory organ is the proboscis gland (not nephridia), making the second claim false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q11 - Relationship between chordates, protochordates, and vertebrates

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All chordates are vertebrates because the notochord is always replaced by a vertebral column in adults.

Statement II: In Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from the head to the tail region and is persistent throughout life.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phylum Chordata is divided into Urochordata, Cephalochordata, and Vertebrata, which differ in the fate of the embryonic notochord.

Step 2: Evaluation
All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates because protochordates (Urochordata and Cephalochordata) never develop a vertebral column; thus, the first claim is false. In Cephalochordata (such as Branchiostoma), the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life, making the second claim true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q12 - Spawning migration in Cyclostomata and buoyancy in Chondrichthyes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cyclostomes are marine ectoparasites on fishes that migrate to fresh water for spawning and die within a few days after spawning.

Statement II: Due to the absence of an air bladder, members of Class Chondrichthyes have to swim constantly to avoid sinking.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cyclostomes and cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) are marine vertebrates with distinct reproductive life cycles and buoyancy mechanisms.

Step 2: Evaluation
Living cyclostomes are ectoparasites on some fishes, live in marine waters, migrate to fresh water for spawning, and die within a few days after spawning, so the first claim is true. Chondrichthyes lack an air bladder and therefore must swim constantly to avoid sinking, so the second claim is also true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q13 - Gill covers, scales, and reproduction in Pisces

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Chondrichthyes, the gill slits are covered by an operculum and the skin is covered with cycloid/ctenoid scales.

Statement II: In Osteichthyes, fertilisation is usually internal and most members are viviparous.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes exhibit opposite patterns with respect to operculum, scale type, fertilisation, and parity.

Step 2: Evaluation
In Chondrichthyes, gill slits are separate without an operculum and the skin contains placoid scales (operculum and cycloid/ctenoid scales belong to Osteichthyes), so the first claim is false. In Osteichthyes, fertilisation is usually external and they are mostly oviparous (internal fertilisation and viviparity in many forms occur in Chondrichthyes), so the second claim is also false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q14 - Heart chambers and fertilisation in Amphibia and Reptilia

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Amphibia, the heart is three-chambered, fertilisation is external, and development is indirect.

Statement II: All reptiles possess a three-chambered heart without exception and undergo external fertilisation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amphibians and reptiles are poikilothermous tetrapods differing in cardiac anatomy and reproductive fertilisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Amphibians have a three-chambered heart (two auricles and one ventricle), external fertilisation, and indirect development, making the first claim true. In Reptilia, the heart is usually three-chambered but is four-chambered in crocodiles, and fertilisation is internal (not external), making the second claim false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q15 - Integument, bones, and physiology of Class Aves

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Class Aves, the skin is moist with numerous sweat glands, and the long bones are solid without air cavities.

Statement II: Birds are homoiothermous and oviparous animals with a completely four-chambered heart and direct development.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Aves exhibits flight adaptations in the integument and skeletal system alongside endothermic (homoiothermous) physiology.

Step 2: Evaluation
In birds, the skin is dry without glands except for the oil gland at the base of the tail, and the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic), making the first claim false. Birds are indeed homoiothermous, oviparous, have a completely four-chambered heart, and show direct development, making the second claim true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_STMT2_Q16 - Parity, thermoregulation, and anatomy of Class Mammalia

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All mammals are strictly viviparous without any exceptions.

Statement II: Mammals are poikilothermous animals that lack external ears (pinnae) and possess a three-chambered heart.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Class Mammalia is characterised by mammary glands, hair, pinnae, a four-chambered heart, homoiothermy, and general viviparity with a notable oviparous exception.

Step 2: Evaluation
While most mammals are viviparous, Ornithorhynchus (platypus) is an oviparous exception, so the first claim is false. Furthermore, mammals are homoiothermous (warm-blooded), possess external ears or pinnae, and have a four-chambered heart, so the second claim is also false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.
